Create.Value.Constant.name: Constant value
Create.Value.Constant.description: Produces the configured Value on every update. Use it as a steady control signal, an arithmetic input, or a simple parameter driver. Other incoming channels remain available.

Create.Value.LFO.name: Oscillator
Create.Value.LFO.summary: Generate a repeating sawtooth, triangle, or sine wave.
Create.Value.LFO.description: Produces a scalar wave from the engine clock using Period and Type. Use it for repeating dimming, modulation, and parameter drivers. It continues independently of UI rendering.

Create.Color.Constant.name: Grayscale constant
Create.Color.Constant.summary: Fill the fixture with a fixed grayscale color.
Create.Color.Constant.description: Converts Value into neutral gray lightness, from black toward white. This is a color source rather than a scalar Constant value, even though both expose a Value parameter.

Create.Color.Color.name: Color
Create.Color.Color.summary: Generate a chosen RGB color and alpha.
Create.Color.Color.description: Produces the selected Color as an output color. Use hexadecimal RGB or RGBA values. The color becomes a fixture result directly, or can feed dimming, inversion, and color combinations.

Create.Layer.Above.name: Layer above
Create.Layer.Above.summary: Read the result of a higher fixture layer.
Create.Layer.Above.description: Copies a previously evaluated higher-layer result into this stack. Layer 0 means the nearest layer above, not absolute attachment layer zero. Use it to modify another layer without replacing its program.

Modify.Value.Invert.name: Invert value
Modify.Value.Invert.summary: Reverse a scalar value around one.
Modify.Value.Invert.description: Writes 1 minus the incoming Value. This turns a rising control into a falling one and reverses normalized modulation. It does not automatically clamp the result.

Modify.Value.Clamp.name: Clamp value
Modify.Value.Clamp.summary: Keep a value inside a minimum and maximum.
Modify.Value.Clamp.description: Restricts the incoming Value to the configured bounds. Values outside the interval stop at an endpoint. Use it to constrain a control range without rescaling values already inside that range.

Modify.Value.MapTo.name: Map output range
Modify.Value.MapTo.summary: Rescale a normalized value into another range.
Modify.Value.MapTo.description: Maps the incoming 0–1 Value to Minimum–Maximum. The normalized input is clamped. Swap the endpoints to reverse the output direction, for example mapping distance intensity from one down to zero.

Modify.Value.MapFromTo.name: Map source to target
Modify.Value.MapFromTo.summary: Map one numeric interval into another.
Modify.Value.MapFromTo.description: Normalizes Value between Source Min and Source Max, then scales it between Minimum and Maximum. Use it for physical distances, controller ranges, and falloff. Out-of-range inputs clamp to the endpoints.

Modify.Value.Steps.name: Quantize steps
Modify.Value.Steps.summary: Turn a continuous value into discrete steps.
Modify.Value.Steps.description: Quantizes incoming Value using Count. Use it for stepped brightness or coarse control changes. This is a numeric transformation; it does not create a timed sequence or stop child evaluation.

Modify.Value.Integrate.name: Accumulate value
Modify.Value.Integrate.summary: Add incoming values over successive updates.
Modify.Value.Integrate.description: Retains an accumulator and adds Value on each evaluation. Reset clears it; Wrap/Clamp selects endpoint behavior. This follows per-update accumulation, not an automatic per-second time integral.

Modify.SampleAndHold.name: Sample and hold
Modify.SampleAndHold.summary: Capture an input bank and hold it.
Modify.SampleAndHold.description: While Sample is true, stores the merged child result. While false, returns the held bank rather than fresh child channels. Children still evaluate; the held output starts empty.

Combine.Add.name: Add
Combine.Add.summary: Add matching channels from ordered inputs.
Combine.Add.description: Adds supported scalar, position, and color channels across child results. The first child determines which channels exist in the result. Use Merge when you want to join distinct channels without arithmetic.

Combine.Multiply.name: Multiply
Combine.Multiply.summary: Multiply matching channels from ordered inputs.
Combine.Multiply.description: Multiplies matching supported channels using the first child’s output domain. Use it to combine scalar modulation signals. For applying a scalar to RGB colors, use Dim color and its Amount driver.

Combine.Crossfade.name: Crossfade
Combine.Crossfade.description: Uses Fader to interpolate across all ordered inputs. At zero it selects the first end; at one it reaches the last. This engine supports linear Shape 0 for scalar, position, and color interpolation.

Filter.Manual.name: Manual gate
Filter.Manual.summary: Pass or suppress an input bank.
Filter.Manual.description: Returns merged input while Open is true, otherwise an empty bank. A closed gate does not stop child oscillators or other retained processes from evaluating. Empty output is distinct from explicit zero.

Convert.Value.ToColor.name: Value to grayscale
Convert.Value.ToColor.summary: Convert a scalar into a grayscale color.
Convert.Value.ToColor.description: Writes a neutral grayscale color from incoming Value, retaining other supported channels. Place it after spatial falloff or scalar effects when the result should become visible fixture light.

Tool.Merge.name: Merge channels
Tool.Merge.summary: Join child banks by overwriting matching channels.
Tool.Merge.description: Combines distinct channels from ordered children into one bank. Later children overwrite earlier values of the same channel. This is not addition, crossfading, or automatic concatenation.

Modify.Color.Invert.name: Invert color
Modify.Color.Invert.description: Uses Value as the inversion amount. Zero keeps the input colors; one moves RGB to its inverse. Use a driver to animate the amount while preserving the rest of the bank.

Modify.Color.Dim.name: Dim color
Modify.Color.Dim.summary: Scale RGB brightness with a scalar amount.
Modify.Color.Dim.description: Multiplies incoming RGB by Amount clamped to 0–1 while preserving alpha. Attach a scalar driver to Amount for LFOs, spatial falloff, or custom control. This Rust extension is distinct from the fixture’s final dimmer.

Create.Position.Constant.name: Position
Create.Position.Constant.summary: Write an XYZ position into the result bank.
Create.Position.Constant.description: Produces a Position channel in metres. Reference-aware distance blocks prefer evaluated positions with setup fallback. A generated Position does not directly rewrite the fixture’s authored scene coordinates.

Create.Reference.Fixture.name: Fixture reference
Create.Reference.Fixture.summary: Refer to another fixture for downstream blocks.
Create.Reference.Fixture.description: Writes a fixture reference selected by stable ID or native-style name. Distance consumes an incoming reference before its own Fixture selector. This carries a reference, not a copy of the target’s colors.

Create.Value.Distance.name: Fixture distance
Create.Value.Distance.summary: Measure distance to a referenced fixture.
Create.Value.Distance.description: Resolves an incoming fixture reference before its Fixture property. The target prefers evaluated Position, then scene position. Auto/Setup controls the source position. The result is Euclidean distance in metres.

Spatial.Distance.name: Spatial distance
Spatial.Distance.summary: Measure distance to a fixture or fixed point.
Spatial.Distance.description: Select a Fixture for live referenced distance, or leave it empty to use Position as a fixed point. An incoming reference takes precedence. The result follows scene movement and can be mapped into light falloff.

Spatial.Axis.name: Axis position
Spatial.Axis.summary: Normalize a fixture’s position along X, Y, or Z.
Spatial.Axis.description: Reads the fixture’s scene coordinate on the selected Axis and maps Minimum–Maximum into 0–1. Use it for directional gradients or to give fixtures different modulation based on their placement.

Script.Value.name: Script value
Script.Value.summary: Evaluate a bounded custom scalar script.
Script.Value.description: Runs a compiled Rhai script with input, t, fixture x/y/z, index, and count. Returns a number under a fixed operation budget. Prefer native blocks for routine maps and effects; use scripting for custom math.

Light.Emitter.name: Light emitter
Light.Emitter.summary: Publish a point, plane or spot light from this fixture.
Light.Emitter.description: Declares a 3D light field attached to this fixture or incoming Position. Point is isotropic; Plane is a finite rectangular area; Spot is a cone. Receivers sample all matching scene emitters in the same frame. Range is finite, Falloff controls attenuation, and Direction sets the plane normal or spot axis. This analytic field does not simulate shadows or scattering.

Light.Receiver.name: Light receiver
Light.Receiver.summary: Sample scene lights at a 3D position.
Light.Receiver.description: Adds matching emitters at the incoming or evaluated fixture Position, including its height. Writes received RGB and scalar intensity. Channel filters light groups; Fixture can restrict the emitter by ID or name. Include Self controls lights on the same fixture. Gain scales the result. Emitters are sampled before receiver-dependent effects; recursive light feedback is not supported.

Create.Position.Current.name: Fixture position
Create.Position.Current.summary: Read this fixture’s authored scene position.
Create.Position.Current.description: Copies this fixture’s setup XYZ coordinates into Position while retaining other incoming channels. Use this as a starting point for spatial effects or to anchor an emitter to its scene placement.

Create.Position.XYZ.name: XYZ position
Create.Position.XYZ.summary: Build Position from three independently driven coordinates.
Create.Position.XYZ.description: Writes a Position from X, Y and Z in metres. Each coordinate accepts a scalar property driver, so native oscillators, random values and Bézier values can animate motion independently on every axis.

Create.Position.Group.Center.name: Group center
Create.Position.Group.Center.summary: Find the center of a fixture group’s bounds.
Create.Position.Group.Center.description: Computes the axis-aligned setup bounds of fixtures in Group and writes their midpoint. An empty Group selects all fixtures; a missing named group produces a diagnostic and no Position.

Create.Position.Group.XYZ.name: Position in group
Create.Position.Group.XYZ.summary: Map normalized XYZ through a group’s bounds.
Create.Position.Group.XYZ.description: Maps X, Y and Z through the selected group’s setup bounds. Padding expands the bounds in metres and Reverse flips the normalized coordinates. Each coordinate can be driven. An empty Group uses all fixtures.

Create.Position.Group.Slide.name: Slide through group
Create.Position.Group.Slide.summary: Animate along one axis of a fixture group.
Create.Position.Group.Slide.description: Moves through the selected group’s bounds on Axis (X=0, Y=1, Z=2), retaining the other center coordinates. Speed maps 0–1 to a 100–0.5 second cycle. Reverse flips direction. The native Speed Audio field must remain zero because no audio provider is installed.

Create.Position.Group.Random.name: Random group motion
Create.Position.Group.Random.summary: Move among seeded random points inside group bounds.
Create.Position.Group.Random.description: Selects repeatable random targets inside expanded group bounds. Speed maps 0–1 to 100–0.2 seconds per target. Continuous interpolates between targets; disabling it jumps. Seed zero derives an independent fixture/node seed. Speed Audio must remain zero. Random sequence and interpolation are defined by this Rust port.

Create.Value.Random.name: Random value
Create.Value.Random.summary: Generate repeatable held or smoothly changing random values.
Create.Value.Random.description: Produces seeded values between zero and one. Interval controls target changes, Randomness jitters that interval, Filter Time interpolates toward each new target, and Pause freezes the generator. Seed zero derives a fixture/node seed; a nonzero seed is explicit. The Rust random sequence and filter are deterministic, not an exact clone of dependency-library randomness.

Modify.Value.RandomizeTrigger.name: Random trigger gate
Modify.Value.RandomizeTrigger.summary: Admit rising-edge triggers according to a probability.
Modify.Value.RandomizeTrigger.description: On each incoming Value rising above 0.5, draws a seeded random value and admits the pulse with Probability. Holds that decision until the input falls. Zero never admits and one always admits. Seed zero derives a fixture/node seed. Uses this port’s deterministic random sequence.

Create.Position.Random.name: Random position
Create.Position.Random.summary: Generate seeded 3D motion inside a box.
Create.Position.Random.description: Selects random XYZ targets between Minimum and Maximum. Interval controls target changes; Filter Time interpolates motion, Randomness jitters the interval, and Pause freezes it. Seed zero derives a fixture/node seed. This native Rust extension is useful for moving light emitters.

Create.Position.Bezier.name: Bézier position
Create.Position.Bezier.summary: Animate a cubic Bézier path through 3D space.
Create.Position.Bezier.description: Evaluates a cubic curve with endpoints P0/P3 and handles P1/P2, all in metres. Progress 0–1 selects a point explicitly; negative Progress uses incoming Value or engine time divided by Duration. Loop repeats and Ping Pong reverses alternate cycles. The inspector offers an X/Z curve editor; numeric vectors retain full 3D control.

Create.Value.Bezier.name: Bézier value
Create.Value.Bezier.summary: Animate a scalar cubic curve for easing and modulation.
Create.Value.Bezier.description: Evaluates a cubic from Start through Control1 and Control2 to End. Progress 0–1 selects an exact point; negative Progress uses incoming Value or engine time divided by Duration. Loop and Ping Pong control clock playback. Use it as an XYZ driver, dimming envelope or emitter parameter driver.
